# testdata/

Golden wire vectors and recorded partition scenarios. Both are checked in from commit
one, and both are part of the specification rather than test fixtures — changing either
requires an ADR in `docs/adr/`.

## `vectors/`

Golden vectors pin the canonical encoding defined in `spec/01-wire-format.md`. Each file
records the input fields, the canonical CBOR, the domain-separated preimage, the BLAKE3
content address, the published signing key seed and the Ed25519 signature.

| Vector | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `observation-note-genesis` | The worked example in §10. Genesis `prev` as a zero-length byte string, an omitted optional field |
| `observation-media-with-geo` | Non-empty `prev`, nonzero `seq`, optional `geo` present, negative microdegrees — the case that would be a float if §2.2 allowed one |
| `attestation-basic` | One node witnessing another's head, signed by the witness |
| `checkpoint-with-frontier` | The only vector with non-integer map keys, pinning the bytewise key ordering rule |

They are generated by `crates/vigil-core/examples/gen_vectors.rs`, which builds every
preimage **by hand from the tables in the spec** and does not call `vigil-core`'s
encoder. A vector produced by the encoder under test proves only that the encoder agrees
with itself; these have to come from the document independently or they are not evidence
of anything.

CI runs the same assertions on the native build and under WASM. That cross-check is the
point: if canonical encoding diverged between the two targets, the same observation would
have two content addresses and the ledger would fork silently — and a native-only test
run cannot see it.

CI also regenerates the vectors and fails if anything changed, so drift between the
generator and the checked-in bytes cannot pass unnoticed.

## `scenarios/`

Seeded `vigil-sim` scripts: partition topologies, clock rollback, equivocation,
withholding, mule routes. Each is reproducible from its seed, so a failure found in CI
replays exactly on a laptop. Not yet written — these land with `vigil-sim`, alongside M1.
